subject: Retention boundary checklist: what interaction artifacts are retained and how to request erasure
messages:
From: Anna Cole <anna.cole@brightbridge.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBridge Security <security@brightbridge.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Retention clarification request — what gets kept by default

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team has a short set of clarifying questions about Redwood's default retention and deletion paths so we can sign off on a pilot. Could you confirm, by artifact type, what is retained by default on hosted accounts (no customer-managed retention settings):

- Raw request text / user prompt (full input)
- Model responses / completions (final output)
- Streaming fragments (partial tokens sent during streaming)
- Intermediate artifacts (KV cache, attention traces, token logs)
- Attachments passed through the API (file blobs or references)
- Telemetry and billing logs (token counts, latencies)

Also: how is EU data residency handled for retention (if our tenant is in eu-central), and what is the standard SLO for completing a deletion/erasure request (including backups and exports)? We will need language we can hand to our legal and ops teams.

Appreciate a concise checklist and the process steps we should expect.

—Anna
Anna Cole
Security PM, BrightBridge
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cole <anna.cole@brightbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-17T17:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention clarification request — what gets kept by default

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise checklist of current default behavior for hosted accounts (summary first, then brief process notes). I've cc'd Marissa (product) and Karthik (policy/infra) for technical and contractual details.

Summary (defaults for hosted Redwood API):
- Raw request text / user prompt: retained 30 days by default. Customers can enable a stricter policy (opt-out) to avoid storing raw prompts.
- Model responses / completions (final output): retained 30 days by default. Finalized outputs are available in exports during that window.
- Streaming fragments: treated as ephemeral; flushed from primary serving cache within 24 hours if not finalized, and purged from transient logs within 7 days.
- Intermediate artifacts (KV cache, attention traces): KV cache is not persisted to long-term storage for normal requests; ephemeral caches exist for session lifetime. Attention traces and raw token-level model internals are not stored as customer-visible persisted artifacts by default.
- Attachments passed through API: attachments referenced by name/metadata are retained for 30 days; raw file blobs follow the same 30-day default unless customer enables auto-delete on upload.
- Telemetry and billing logs: raw request-level telemetry (for debugging) is retained 7 days; aggregated billing/usage records (token counts per invoice period) are retained 365 days for accounting and audit. These aggregated records do not include full prompt text.

Process notes / deletion SLOs:
- Self-service deletion: Customers can issue a scoped erase request via the Console or Support portal. For default hosted tenants, we perform deletions across primary stores within 72 hours and across backups within 30 days.
- Evidence and audit id: After completion we provide a deletion confirmation package (audit id + affected shards list) suitable for vendor assessments.
- Legal holds & exceptions: Deletion SLOs pause for lawful retention or active legal holds; we surface that in the confirmation email.
- EU residency: If your tenant is configured for eu-central, persisted artifacts (requests/completions/attachments) are stored in eu region primary stores. Deletion follows same SLOs (72 hours primary, 30 days for backups) and we ensure no copies are replicated to other regions unless explicitly configured for cross-region failover.

Attachments: I attached a simple retention matrix (retention_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a redacted sample export (sample_export_redacted.json) that shows fields included in exports.

If helpful, Karthik can add the internal runbook link and the technical distinctions between transient logs and persisted artifacts.

Next steps: Would you like a one-page statement we can include in your procurement packet (shorter than an SLA) summarizing these points?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Security — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cole <anna.cole@brightbridge.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T01:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention clarification request — what gets kept by default

Adding a few technical clarifications to Lauren's checklist so your infra team can map to their controls: 

- Streaming fragments vs finalized completions: when a streaming request completes (HTTP stream closed or final token signaled), the final completion is recorded in the same 30-day bucket as non-streamed outputs. Partial fragments that never finalize are treated as transient and are removed from hot storage within 24 hours; a compacted log entry (non-content metadata: request id, timestamps, byte counts) may persist for up to 7 days for troubleshooting.

- KV cache and model state: session-level KV caches are kept in-memory and flushed when the session ends. We do have an opt-in session-persistence feature for Dedicated/Private customers — that changes retention and is explicitly controlled by customer configuration.

- Backups and replicas: backups are immutable snapshots on a rolling schedule; deletion requests enqueue the affected keys for expunge. The 30-day backup SLO accounts for the usual snapshot cycle; cryptographic shredding of keys is used where hardware supports it.

- Attachments: our API stores attachments as object-store blobs. If your integration uploads PII files and you want immediate purge, please enable the "auto-delete-on-upload" flag we can set at the tenant level; otherwise standard 30-day retention applies.

- Telemetry anonymization: token-level billing logs are hashed and aggregated before long-term storage; raw token strings are not kept in aggregated stores. For PCI/SOC evidence requests we can provide aggregated reports without prompt contents.

Runbook / audit link: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-412 (contains the erase workflow and audit-id format).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure PM — Redwood Inference
